checks.describe: the MCP server (labs/opsmate/mcp/mcp_k8s.py) is a stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 server implementing initialize/tools/list/tools/call with exactly two READ-ONLY tools (get_pod_status, get_pod_logs) — and NO mutating verb (create/delete/patch/scale/apply) exists in it at all (the visitor-badge discipline as tool design) (Lab Step 3)
checks.run: F=labs/opsmate/mcp/mcp_k8s.py; if python3 -c "import ast,sys; ast.parse(open('$F').read())" 2>/dev/null && grep -q 'initialize' "$F" && grep -q 'tools/list' "$F" && grep -q 'tools/call' "$F" && grep -q 'get_pod_status' "$F" && grep -q 'get_pod_logs' "$F" && grep -q 'jsonrpc' "$F" && ! grep -Eq 'kubectl[^)]*(delete|create|patch|scale|apply|edit)|"(delete|create|patch|scale|apply|edit)"' "$F"; then echo mcp-readonly-ok; else echo mcp-readonly-wrong; fi

checks.describe: agent.py is the teaching artifact: it spawns the MCP server, converts MCP schemas to OpenAI tool schemas (name/description/inputSchema -> parameters — the USB-C beat), offers tools on turn 1, executes tool calls via MCP, and OMITS tools on the answer turn (the loop fix — the load-bearing single line). It also carries a system nudge to gather both status and logs (Lab Steps 4-7)
checks.run: F=labs/m13/agent.py; if python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('$F').read())" 2>/dev/null && grep -q 'mcp_k8s.py' "$F" && grep -q '"parameters": t\["inputSchema"\]' "$F" && grep -q '"tools": tools' "$F" && grep -q 'chat({"messages": msgs, "think": False, "max_tokens": 1200})' "$F" && grep -qi 'omit' "$F" && grep -qi 'gather BOTH' "$F"; then echo agent-loop-fix-ok; else echo agent-loop-fix-wrong; fi

checks.describe: crashloop.yaml is the DESIGNED subject: namespace shop + a busybox payments-api Deployment that logs the FATAL db-connection line and exits 1 (the diagnosable crashloop the agent reads back). No model server — the cluster is the subject, not the server (Lab Step 2)
checks.run: F=labs/m13/crashloop.yaml; if python3 -c "import yaml; list(yaml.safe_load_all(open('$F')))" 2>/dev/null && grep -q 'namespace: shop' "$F" && grep -q 'payments-api' "$F" && grep -q 'FATAL' "$F" && grep -q 'busybox' "$F" && grep -q 'exit 1' "$F"; then echo crashloop-ok; else echo crashloop-wrong; fi

checks.describe: the slim Part-A cluster (opsmate-agent, one bare node) is up via the isolated kubeconfig and the crashloop pod is applied and crashing — the live state the MCP server inspects. Self-seeds: creates the bare cluster and applies crashloop.yaml if absent (Lab Steps 1-2)
checks.run: export KUBECONFIG=labs/opsmate/k8s/kubeconfig; kind get clusters 2>/dev/null | grep -qx opsmate-agent || kind create cluster --name opsmate-agent --kubeconfig labs/opsmate/k8s/kubeconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready nodes --all --timeout=120s >/dev/null 2>&1; kubectl get ns shop >/dev/null 2>&1 || kubectl apply -f labs/m13/crashloop.yaml >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 25; if kubectl -n shop get pods 2>/dev/null | grep -q payments-api; then echo crashloop-live; else echo crashloop-not-live; fi

checks.describe: the MCP server, driven by hand (printf JSON-RPC lines | mcp_k8s.py), returns serverInfo on initialize, a 2-tool list on tools/list, and the REAL pod row on tools/call against the live crashloop — proving the read-only inspector works end to end vs the isolated kubeconfig (Lab Step 3)
checks.run: export KUBECONFIG=labs/opsmate/k8s/kubeconfig; kubectl get ns shop >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo mcp-no-cluster; exit 0; }; OUT=$(printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_pod_status","arguments":{"namespace":"shop","pod":"payments-api"}}}' | python3 labs/opsmate/mcp/mcp_k8s.py 2>/dev/null); if echo "$OUT" | grep -q 'opsmate-k8s-inspector' && echo "$OUT" | grep -q 'get_pod_status' && echo "$OUT" | grep -q 'payments-api'; then echo mcp-live-ok; else echo mcp-live-wrong; fi

checks.describe: the lab teaches the full agentic arc: drive MCP by hand, run the agent (decide -> execute -> ground), EXHIBIT A (the loop — tools left in, spend rows accumulate), EXHIBIT B (tool_choice:none silently dropped), the omit-tools fix, arg hygiene, and the Spend + K8s lens moment — then Part B the capstone and a FULL teardown (Lab Steps 3-16)
checks.run: F=site/docs/m13-agentic-capstone/lab.md; if grep -q 'get_pod_status' "$F" && grep -qi 'EXHIBIT A' "$F" && grep -qi 'EXHIBIT B' "$F" && grep -q 'tool_choice' "$F" && grep -qi 'omit the tools' "$F" && grep -qi 'arg hygiene' "$F" && grep -qi 'Spend lens' "$F" && grep -q '1.2.0' "$F" && grep -qi 'gate.sh' "$F" && grep -qi 'portfolio' "$F" && grep -qi 'teardown' "$F"; then echo lab-arc-ok; else echo lab-arc-incomplete; fi

checks.describe: the capstone assets exist: the new cache-eviction runbook (the v1.2 training signal) and the portfolio skeleton (README with the 5-row rubric, MODELKIT.md by digest, an eval-report template, and dirs for manifests/dashboards/ci/eval-report) the learner fills and publishes (Lab Steps 10, 15)
checks.run: R=labs/m13/cache-eviction.md; P=labs/m13/portfolio; if grep -qi 'eviction' "$R" && grep -qi 'redis' "$R" && test -f "$P/README.md" && grep -qi 'rubric' "$P/README.md" && test -f "$P/MODELKIT.md" && grep -qi 'digest' "$P/MODELKIT.md" && test -d "$P/manifests" && test -d "$P/dashboards" && test -d "$P/ci" && test -d "$P/eval-report"; then echo portfolio-ok; else echo portfolio-wrong; fi

checks.describe: the lesson places the progression (naive RAG -> agentic RAG -> tool-using -> multi-agent), teaches structured outputs as the reliability primitive FIRST, tool-calling ops implications (latency/loops/cost), MCP in 30 min (USB-C), the guarded agent (read-only + spend), the capstone narrative, and the course wrap with the 303-agentops hand-off — with >=2 Mermaid diagrams (Lesson)
checks.run: F=site/docs/m13-agentic-capstone/lesson.md; M=$(grep -c '```mermaid' "$F"); if grep -qi 'naive RAG' "$F" && grep -qi 'agentic RAG' "$F" && grep -qi 'multi-agent' "$F" && grep -qi 'reliability primitive' "$F" && grep -qi 'USB-C' "$F" && grep -qi 'visitor badge' "$F" && grep -qi '303-agentops' "$F" && [ "$M" -ge 2 ]; then echo lesson-ok; else echo lesson-incomplete; fi
